lessons.title: Hear pāchhe milsū — see you later

segments.text: Ask how someone is, answer hū̃ ṭhīk hū̃, then say राम राम सा once. Close the text before the new parting line begins.
pāchhe milsū — see you later.
Hear two groups: pā-chhe | mil-sū. The first points later/back; the second carries meeting again. Listen twice, tap the two groups, and say them once. Do not spell the line yet.
Choose the cue that promises another meeting, not the cue that starts a conversation. Answer it with pāchhe milsū.
Say the two sound groups once, then stop.
Source: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 2.

segments.prompt: You hear pāchhe milsū at the end of a conversation. What does it promise?

feedback.correct: Right: it points to meeting again later.
feedback.incorrect: This is the taught see-you-later line.

lessons.title: छ (chha) — one aspirated consonant
lessons.gloss: the Devanagari consonant sign for aspirated chha

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one sign until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write नाम, say pāchhe once, then write known ठ. The new sign carries a different consonant and keeps the released breath.
छ — chha.
Keep the sign visible. Finger-trace the main body first and add the headline last. Say chha with a small breath after the consonant.
Trace छ (chha) once, copy it once, then cover the model and write it once.
Write छ (chha) once from memory.
Source: Unicode Devanagari chart.

segments.prompt: Which sound does छ (chha) carry in the taught farewell?

feedback.incorrect: Read this sign as chha, with a small breath.

segments.text: Complete mhāro nām Rām hai, write छ (chha), then write known ू. Today's mark attaches above a consonant instead.
े — dependent e छ (chha) + े = छे — chhe.
The mark cannot stand as the word's consonant. Add it above and to the right of छ (chha); read the result chhe.
Copy छे twice. Point to the consonant, then to the vowel mark.
Cover the model and write छे once.
Source: Unicode Devanagari chart.

segments.prompt: Which vowel mark turns छ (chha) into छे?

lessons.title: ि — written before, heard after
lessons.gloss: the dependent short-i vowel sign, written before its consonant

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one vowel mark until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write है, then known म and the long-ī mark from णी. The new mark is short i and has a placement rule worth noticing.
ि — dependent short i म + ि = मि — mi.
The visible mark sits to the left of म, but the sound follows the consonant: read मि as mi, never im.
Build मि twice. Each time, point left-to-right on the page, then say the sounds in their spoken order: m-i.
Write मि once from memory.
Source: Unicode Devanagari chart.

segments.prompt: The short-i mark is visible before म. How do you read मि?

feedback.correct: Right: the mark is written before but pronounced after the consonant.
feedback.incorrect: Read consonant then vowel: मि is mi.

segments.text: Write the full my-name statement, then ask and answer wellbeing once. Write मि and known न. Today adds only ल (la).
ल — la.
Keep the sign visible. Trace the open lower body before adding the headline. Say la once the hand stops.
Copy ल (la) once beside the model. Cover it, wait five seconds, and write it once.
Read ल (la) once, then stop.
Source: Unicode Devanagari chart.

segments.prompt: Write the Devanagari consonant sign for la.

feedback.incorrect: Repair the open lower body, then add the headline: ल.

lessons.title: पाछे मिलसू (pāchhe milsū) — assemble the two sound groups
lessons.gloss: see you later, assembled from known written units

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — join only known units until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Say thāro, then write हूं ठीक हूं and circle ठ. Say pāchhe | milsū, then write छे, मि, and ल (la) separately.
पा | छे मि | ल (la) | सू पाछे मिलसू (pāchhe milsū).
Nothing new hides in the join. Read the two groups, then write them with one space between.
Cover the romanization. Read पाछे मिलसू (pāchhe milsū), cover the line, wait ten seconds, and write it once.
Point to the short-i mark and say why it appears before म on the page.
Source: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 2.

segments.prompt: From pāchhe | milsū, write the complete two-word phrase.

feedback.correct: Both sound groups are complete with one space between.
feedback.incorrect: Repair one known block at a time: पा | छे मि | ल | सू.

segments.text: Write थ, then say राम राम सा once as the common farewell.
राम राम सा. — goodbye / farewell पाछे मिलसू (pāchhe milsū). — see you later.
The second line explicitly points to meeting later. Other regions and relationships may choose another parting line; this payoff scores only the two source-attested choices it taught.
Listen: hear one line and identify common farewell or see-you-later.
Speak: answer a later-meeting cue with pāchhe milsū.
Read: match both printed lines to their meanings.
Write: hear pāchhe milsū, wait ten seconds, and write it without a model.
Score all four separately. A spoken line does not replace missing writing.
Stop after one accurate four-skill pass.
Sources: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 2 and SIL International, Marwari–English Dictionary archive.

segments.prompt: From sound alone, write see you later, then say the common farewell aloud.

feedback.correct: Writing and speech complete the two parting intentions.
feedback.incorrect: Repair पाछे | मिलसू, then say राम राम सा aloud.
